provider.description: Provider routing override. `kling` (alias `klingai`) runs native Kling with no fallback; `fal` runs the fal.ai mirror; `auto` (default) uses the Kling -> fal.ai fallback chain. Case-insensitive.

prompt.description: Text prompt. Refer to the reference images as @Image1, @Image2, … and to the elements as @Element1, @Element2, ….

image_urls.description: Reference images (1-10): URLs or Base64 data URIs. Max 30MB each, at least 300px per side, aspect ratio 0.4-2.5. Each reference image and each element adds a small per-request charge.

reference_image_urls.description: Additional views of the element from other angles (1-3).

elements.description: Characters or objects to keep consistent, referred to in the prompt as @Element1, @Element2, … (up to 7). Images and elements together: at most 10.

result_type.description: `single` returns independent images (`num_images` of them); `series` returns a coherent set of related images (`series_amount` of them).

num_images.description: Number of independent images to generate (1-9). Used when result_type is `single`.

series_amount.description: Number of images in the series (2-10). Used when result_type is `series`.

resolution.description: Output resolution: 2K, 4K or 8K (a 1:1 image is 2048, 4096 or 8192 px a side). The price per image depends on it.

aspect_ratio.description: Aspect ratio of the generated images (width:height). `auto` lets the model pick it from the prompt and the references.

url.description: The URL where the file can be downloaded from.

b64_json.description: The base64-encoded JSON of the generated image.

credits_used.description: The number of tokens consumed during generation.

usd_spent.description: The total amount of money spent by the user in USD.

x-codeSamples.source:
curl --request POST \
  --url 'https://api.aimlapi.com/v1/images/generations' \
  --header 'Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_AIMLAPI_KEY>' \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"model": "klingai/image-v4-image-to-image", "prompt": "Describe what you want the model to generate.", "image_urls": ["https://example.com/input.jpg"]}'
